title: Canetti takes Armstrong on tour; Pete du Conge leads
summary: Canetti signed Armstrong and had Pete du Conge assemble his band; Briggs received a wire from Canetti but did not answer, and recalls du Conge's New Orleans clarinet background.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: somewhat in Paris, then he signed a contract with Canetti.
How did that come about?

Well, he signed a contract with Canetti, and Canetti take him on a tour.

And immediately I had a wire from Canetti asking me -- could I come immediately. And I didn't answer.

It happened that he also left Canetti. Whatever happened, it was a question of money.

But when I saw Pete, when Pete came back to Paris, he said -- well, I'm glad -- well, I explained to him that I'd gotten a wire from Canetti and everything, and he wasn't aware of it, he didn't know anything about it.

So, I told him, I said that in any case, I said, 'You don't have to worry, I would never do such a thing.'
Briggs

He said, 'Well, I didn't think that you would.' He knew me that well, you see. He said, 'I didn't know anything about it, but I didn't think you would, accept something, -- And, Louie came back to Paris, and he stayed around for a little while, and then he went back to America. That's where Canetti's idea come in, to have me record here, with Bricktop's band. He came up and heard us several times, 'cause he was a friend of Pete anyhow. Pete was in charge of the orchestra.
Well, in other words, just let me get some of this straight. I'm getting confused about some of this.
Yes.
In other words, when Armstrong went out -- Canetti took Armstrong out, and he got Pete Du Conge to --
To lead the orchestra.
Briggs 266
To be strawboss on the band?
Yes.
Right. And Du Conge got the musicians, or did Canetti get --
Yes, yeh. He had a pretty nice band. He had a pretty nice band together -- for Louie, that accompanied Louie.
And there's nothing in the world that Pete wouldn't do for Louie, as you know.
Sure.
So --
Well, had Pete known Louie back in the old days in New Orleans?
I don't think that he did, because Pete was a little younger than we were.
Okay.
I believe that I'm one year younger than Louie. Yes, early 1900.
Briggs 267
Yes, that's right.
Uh huh. And Pete was much younger.
He was.
But he knew of Louie in New Orleans, because he often told me how he started playing the clarinet, and Tio -- you ever heard of Tio? *
Sure.
Tio gave him pointers in the thing. So, --
